claude.sample_unit: ICU patients (MIMIC-IV development cohort; eICU external cohort)

links.outcome: Model performance when generalized from MIMIC-IV to eICU hospitals
links.effect: Common-feature Random Forest on eICU achieved AUC 0.743 (95% CI 0.738-0.749), versus LSTM AUC 0.884 on MIMIC-IV held-out test set.
links.quote: Because three development-model predictors (vasopressors, mechanical ventilation, and the full SOFA score) are not consistently recorded in eICU, cross-institutional generalization is assessed with a common-feature Random Forest, yielding AUC 0.743 (95% CI: 0.738-0.749).

links.outcome: Per-hospital fairness variability in cross-institutional eICU audit
links.effect: Measurable per-hospital variability: TPR gap 0.134, FPR gap 0.060, FOR gap 0.032.
links.quote: A cross-institutional eICU fairness audit reveals measurable per-hospital variability (TPR gap 0.134, FPR gap 0.060, FOR gap 0.032); subgroup estimates are reported with event counts and Wilson intervals.

links.outcome: Final TPR gaps under dynamic adaptive fairness versus static reweighing versus no intervention across retraining cycles
links.effect: No significant difference in final TPR gaps across three strategies (Friedman chi2(2)=1.195, p=0.550); adaptive controller showed damped trajectories vs larger transient spikes with static reweighing.
links.quote: Across 30 independent runs, all three strategies converge to final TPR gaps with no significant difference (Friedman $\chi ^{2}(2)=1.195$, $p=0.550$); however, the Dynamic Adaptive Fairness controller exhibits bounded, damped trajectories where static reweighing shows larger transient spikes.

links.outcome: Post-covariate-shift TPR-gap spike with adaptive control versus no intervention
links.effect: Adaptive control attenuated post-shift TPR-gap spike (Δ=+0.091) relative to no-intervention baseline (Δ=+0.139).
links.quote: Under an auxiliary exogenous covariate shift, adaptive control attenuates the post-shift TPR-gap spike ($\Delta =+0.091$) relative to the no-intervention baseline ($\Delta =+0.139$).

links.outcome: Discrimination of LSTM versus tabular baselines and SOFA-only baseline on same data
links.effect: LSTM AUC 0.884 comparable to LightGBM 0.892, RF 0.889, XGBoost 0.886, LR 0.867 and well above SOFA-only 0.770.
links.quote: Using the MIMIC-IV cohort, the LSTM achieves an AUC of 0.884 (95% CI: 0.859-0.908) on a held-out test set, comparable to contemporary tabular baselines (LightGBM 0.892, Random Forest 0.889, XGBoost 0.886, Logistic Regression 0.867) and substantially above a SOFA-only clinical baseline (0.770).
